title: Defining jazz: blues, funerals and not only New Orleans
summary: Sam defines jazz as music from within yourself and tells of Tampa funeral marches and the return jam.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well you led into two questions and the two questions I--and that's what you said, I'd like to uh,

to focus you on, if I may. The first one was, why do you think--first of all--what is jazz? What is your definition of jazz? Cause I see it to be one of the things that causes problems, you know, like that leaves it open for--like you mentioned WRVR coming in saying that they're playing jazz. I mean, it seems like they had some problems in defining what jazz is--what, what is jazz? In your definition?

What is jazz? Well, I can only relate it to what--and, they used to tell me it's uh, it's a music that comes from within yourself. You express yourself when you're down--went from the blues which uh, we had plenty of during the slavery time, I understand that it was the music that, that uh our forefathers played; sad blues which expressed their feelings of what was going on at that time what, what-- on up to--where to uh, the happy feelings when, like on Saturday night, you know, when they have the dances and--I mean the little dances over across the field, all the way over across--over there in the little shack, you know, the bands be , be , you know, uh, uh, expressing themselves, the music uh, for themselves. You see that's the best way I-I can understand it, I-I can explain it. It's like, uh, a funeral, you know, like in, in the South, the people in the Northern states didn't, never expressed uh, uh, never, uh had these things happen in the North but like in funerals--uh, even where I came from in Florida when I was coming up--in fact I played a

Oh, so you did that in Florida, too?
So what happened in other places, other than just New Orleans--
Sure. That's good for the record. Sure man.
A lot of people want to pigeon-hole certain things to certain areas and think that's the only place it happened, you know, like jazz was, quote, un-quote, born in New Orleans--

No, sir. No, sir. That happened in Tampa, where I came up in Tampa, Florida; now, whether they do that now I--or not, you know, I don't know.
